holidays.name: Johnny Appleseed Day
holidays.description: A day honoring the barefoot, tin-pot-hatted legend who wandered America planting apple trees. Celebrate by eating apples, baking pies, or planting a tree.
holidays.origin: Honors John Chapman, born September 26, 1774. Some observe it on March 11, the date traditionally linked to his death in 1845, while others celebrate on his birthday in September.
holidays.funFact: Many of Johnny Appleseed's apples were not for eating. They were small, tart 'spitters' mostly used to make hard cider, which was the popular drink on the frontier.

holidays.name: Plant a Flower Day
holidays.description: A day for getting your hands dirty and sticking some blossoms in the ground, brightening up your yard, balcony, or windowsill as spring approaches.
holidays.origin: An informal gardening observance that grew out of early spring planting traditions and is promoted by garden centers and flower enthusiasts.
holidays.funFact: Sunflowers can track the sun across the sky when young, a movement called heliotropism, so a planted sunflower really does follow the light.

holidays.name: Worship of Tools Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day to show appreciation for your trusty hammers, wrenches, and screwdrivers. Give your tools some love by cleaning, oiling, and organizing them.
holidays.origin: A humorous, informal observance among DIYers and handy folks. It nods to the real tool-worshipping traditions of Ayudha Puja in India, where tools and instruments are honored.
holidays.funFact: The oldest known stone tools are about 3.3 million years old, found in Kenya, which predates the earliest known members of our own genus, Homo.

holidays.name: Panic Day
holidays.description: A day for letting loose a little controlled freak-out and then laughing at how much you worried. Think of it as a permission slip to run around in circles for a minute.
holidays.origin: An unofficial and lighthearted observance, often tied to the idea of releasing stress and recognizing that panic is a normal human reaction.
holidays.funFact: The word 'panic' comes from Pan, the Greek god of the wild, whose sudden shouts in the woods were said to cause irrational terror in travelers and animals.

holidays.name: Oatmeal Nut Waffles Day
holidays.description: A cozy breakfast holiday dedicated to waffles studded with oats and crunchy nuts. Fire up the waffle iron and top them with syrup, fruit, or butter.
holidays.origin: A food-calendar observance popularized by recipe sites and breakfast lovers, celebrating a hearty twist on the classic waffle.
holidays.funFact: Waffle irons were patented in the US in 1869 by Cornelius Swarthout, long after medieval Europeans were cooking waffles between ornate patterned iron plates.
